title: Product Designer
description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

Imagine yourself in the 1970s or 80s thinking through how computing should look and feel for people who had never seen one before. That's what we're trying to do at Notion — make software that feels timeless, with the craftsmanship of German cameras, playfulness of Japanese toys, and mass appeal of Coca-Cola. We have no end of fascinating challenges that can only be solved by someone with innate product & UX sense, technical aptitude, great taste, and impeccable craft.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve



- Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential.
- Craft every detail of new product features, from idea to UX to pixel-perfect execution.
- Run projects end to end with engineers to drive your vision to the ship line.
- Partner closely with our Customer Experience, Sales, and Customer Success teams to understand what each of our diverse user segments need, want, and love about Notion. Use this data and acquired intuition to prioritize, plan, and scope our product roadmap.
- Work with Marketing to devise new ways to tell great stories throughout the user lifecycle, and across our site, product, help guides and other channels.
- Create new patterns that are intuitive, practical, and convergent. Evolve our design system intentionally as we scale.

Skills You'll Need To Bring



- You have well-rounded skills and experience to run projects independently end to end. 5+ years of working experience.
- You seek to understand the needs of customers then explore and advocate for the strongest user experiences to solve their problems
- You enjoy untangling vague conceptual problems and have a sharp intuition for the most accessible mental models and flows, so users can immediately start gaining value out of the product.
- You create clear, intuitive, and visually appealing human interfaces

We're looking for a Product Design Engineer to help define what comes next.

- What entirely new products should Citizen build next?
- How can we prototype and validate ideas in days instead of months?

NODA is a veteran-owned, venture-backed technology company that is transforming how unmanned systems collaborate in complex, mission-critical environments. title: Design Technologist
description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for startups. Open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

The Role

Rho is hiring Design Technologists — people who design products by building them. You lead with taste and user intuition, but you work in the medium: prototyping in code, leveraging AI tools, getting to real signal before anyone's written a PRD. You're not waiting for requirements. You're generating them.

The design role has more leverage than it's ever had. AI is compressing the space between insight and artifact. A designer who can prototype in code, think in systems, and build deep customer intuition can now shape product in ways that weren't possible two years ago. This role exists to capture that.

At Rho, you'll own product problems from first principles through shipped software. You'll be the person in the room who knows the customer cold, has the design judgment to know what's right, and has the technical fluency to prove it fast. This role is for someone who's already working this way — and wants a company that's building around it.

What You'll Do

Design by making. Own complex product areas end-to-end. Use functional prototypes — not decks — as your primary tool for thinking, aligning, and deciding. Work in high fidelity early. Ship the concept, not just the comp.

Know the customer. Build real expertise in how founders and early-stage companies manage money. Use research when it's right, but also trust the pattern recognition that comes from sustained proximity to the problem.

Set product direction. Your design judgment is a strategic input, not a downstream service. Shape what gets built, what gets cut, and what gets rethought. Bring clarity to ambiguity. Say no to the right things.

Hold an unreasonable standard for craft. Usability, interaction quality, visual refinement — every detail in a banking product earns or erodes trust. Sweat accordingly.

Work AI-native. Use AI tools to accelerate your own process. Identify where AI belongs in the product experience itself. Help the team build new workflows as the old ones stop making sense.

Push the system forward. Evolve Rho's design system — not just components, but the principles that make a complex financial platform feel simple.

Who You Are



- 4+ years designing digital products. A portfolio that shows exceptional craft and end-to-end ownership — not just the pretty screens, but evidence that you shaped the outcome. Fintech is a plus, not a gate.
- You prototype beyond Figma — in code, with AI tools, in whatever gets you to a better answer faster. You're not an engineer, but you're not afraid of the material.
- You work autonomously and thrive in ambiguity. You plan your own work. You don't need to be managed toward quality.
- You design for real complexity — edge cases, dense workflows, the unglamorous stuff that separates good products from great ones.

description:
Req187052

Position Purpose

At The Home Depot, we get UX; it is baked into our DNA. Now we are expanding our team to drive new initiatives. As a member of the UX team, you will work with other strategists, designers, and researchers to help craft end-to-end experiences and identify customer needs.

You are a designer with a desire to solve interesting and meaty customer problems. Whether it's using design thinking techniques to drive ideation and alignment or bringing a paper prototype to your user for a quick experiment, you can identify and execute the right steps towards solving a problem. You might not consider yourself a researcher, but you have solid awareness of research best practices and know that research is the foundation towards good design. You appreciate feedback and support from fellow researchers, designers, engineers, analysts, or product managers in our cross functional environment. title: Product Designer
description:
Product Designer
 Job Summary
We’re looking for a Product Designer to help shape and execute the product experience for RedSail RxMarket. This role will focus on designing intuitive, high-impact workflows across our B2B marketplace, helping pharmacies and medical practices discover products, compare options, place orders, and manage purchasing with confidence. You’ll report to the Director of Product Management and work closely with engineers, product partners, and cross-functional stakeholders on high-priority marketplace initiatives. This is a hands-on role for a designer who is comfortable owning work end-to-end, from discovery and research through high-fidelity execution and launch. You will lead the end-to-end design process for key marketplace workflows, partnering closely with Product Management, Engineering, Business Analytics, Customer Support, and Marketing to deliver intuitive, scalable solutions across both buyer and supplier experiences.
 What You’ll Do

- Own the design process for key initiatives from discovery and concepting through wireframes, high-fidelity designs, and handoff
- Design intuitive, scalable experiences for complex B2B marketplace workflows including search, comparison, ordering, checkout, post-purchase, and supplier-side tools
- Partners with Product Management, Engineering, Business Analytics, Customer Support, and Marketing to turn user and business needs into thoughtful design solutions
- Conduct and synthesize user research, including interviews, usability testing, and workflow validation, to inform product decisions
- Create user flows, wireframes, prototypes, and polished UI designs with a high level of independence
- Contribute to and evolve design patterns and systems to improve consistency and quality across the product
- Advocate for user-centered design while balancing speed, technical constraints, and business goals
- Participate in design reviews and provide constructive feedback to improve overall product quality
 Education/Training

- Bachelor’s degree in design, communications design, UX design, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
 Required Work Experience/Skills

- 4+ years of experience as a UI / UX Designer, Product Designer, or similar design role in a technology company
- Strong experience designing ecommerce, marketplace, or transactional products, ideally in a B2B or B2B2C environment
- Proven ability to work autonomously and own design deliverables from start to finish
- Comfort operating in ambiguous problem spaces and turning loosely defined requirements into clear, usable solutions
- Solid foundation in UX principles, interaction design, and visual design
- Hands-on experience conducting user research and usability testing, and applying insights to design decisions
- Proficiency with modern design tools such as Figma and strong collaboration skills with engineers
- Ability to clearly articulate design decisions and trade-offs

title: Product Designer
description:
Reducto is the agentic document platform for leading AI teams who demand enterprise performance at scale. We provide a comprehensive toolkit for working with documents the way a human would, combining custom in-house and leading frontier models to power efficient and accurate document workflows.

We’ve grown rapidly, increasing revenue 8x year over year and partnering with hundreds of companies, from leading AI teams like Harvey, Vanta, and Scale, to enterprise customers across FAANG and top trading firms.

Reducto has raised over $100M from world-class investors including a16z, Benchmark, and First Round Capital.

The Opportunity

As an early member of our product design team you’ll shape the foundation of how users interact with our product—from core workflows to visual language. You’ll work directly with our CEO, engineers, and customers to design entirely new experiences. We don’t have PMs— so you’ll own design end-to-end: user research, UX flows, wireframes, high-fidelity mocks, and design systems.

We Would Love To Meet You If



- You are your own worst critic. You have a high bar for quality and don’t rest until the job is done right—no settling for 90%. We want someone who ships fast, with high agency, and who doesn't just voice problems but actively jumps in to fix them.
- You’ve shipped complex products before for 2+ years, ideally for engineers, researchers, or ops-heavy teams.
- You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and defining structure where none exists.
- You move fast, but also care deeply about polish and craft.

The Core Work Will Include



- Lead design end-to-end for Reducto, owning everything from defining a world-class brand to shipping beautiful experiences that users love.
- Develop brand new products and user workflows.
- Build and own our design system, brand, and how we present ourselves to the world.
- Obsess over the small details, driving a culture that highly values design.

Bonus Points If You



- Have prior experience founding a company or building products at early stages
- Are ambitious and driven, and care a lot about doing great work with great people
- Keep up with the latest developments in ML/AI

Benefits



- Unlimited PTO: We believe great work requires recharging.

- Reimbursed Transportation: Provide us with your receipts and we’ll take care of the costs

- Parental Leave: Work with us to build a leave schedule that works for you and your family

This is an in person role at our office in SF. We’re an early stage company which means that the role requires working hard and moving quickly. Please only apply if that excites you.

About Novig

Novig is building America's #1 sports prediction market. Our mission is to financialize and democratize sports trading - taking a closed system run by casinos and turning it into a fair, efficient, two-sided market where the power sits with users.

With Novig recently becoming a CFTC-designated market — the fastest designation of its kind in US history— we're bringing the prediction market built for sports fans nationwide.

We're backed by some of Silicon Valley's top investors — Pantera, Forerunner, Lux, NFX, Paul Graham, and Joe Montana — who have collectively invested over $100M behind this vision.

About The Role

We’re hiring a Product Designer at Novig to help craft the core experience of the best sports prediction market in the world.

This is a high-ownership role with real scope, autonomy, and influence over the direction of the product. You'll work directly with the VP of Design, founder, and core product team, shaping the product end-to-end — from understanding users, concepting new product features, and helping frame product direction to shipping precise, polished interfaces.

Who You Are And What You Will Do



- You build what users love. You design experiences that feel intuitive, rewarding, and differentiated, deepening how fans engage with sports trading.
- You make complexity feel simple. You turn sports markets, live data, and trading mechanics into clear, fast, and engaging product experiences.
- You validate ideas fast. You rapidly concept, prototype, test, and iterate to produce the highest-impact solutions, pushing for the highest quality execution, thoughtful interaction design, and strong product thinking across every surface and flow.
- You help evolve our system. You define, grow, and maintain our design system to keep our product cohesive as it grows.
- You have 3–4+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio that shows system-level thinking, strong attention to detail, and tangible business impact — backed by excellent visual and interaction design skills and deep Figma fluency.
- You have a sharp instinct for user behavior and what makes products click, with strong product judgment grounded in real customer understanding.
- You have a strong point of view on design systems — you think in components, tokens, and variants.
- You're AI-forward, with a strong interest in actively integrating AI into design workflows.
- You move quickly and adapt well in fast-paced environments, with a bias toward ownership and action, clear and thoughtful communication, and genuine curiosity about markets.
- Bonus: you have experience in fintech, sports betting, trading, or other data-rich consumer products.

title: Product Designer
description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

Imagine yourself in the 1970s or 80s thinking through how computing should look and feel for people who had never seen one before. That's what we're trying to do at Notion — make software that feels timeless, with the craftsmanship of German cameras, playfulness of Japanese toys, and mass appeal of Coca-Cola. We have no end of fascinating challenges that can only be solved by someone with innate product & UX sense, technical aptitude, great taste, and impeccable craft.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve



- Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential.
- Craft every detail of new product features, from idea to UX to pixel-perfect execution.
- Run projects end to end with engineers to drive your vision to the ship line.
- Partner closely with our Customer Experience, Sales, and Customer Success teams to understand what each of our diverse user segments need, want, and love about Notion. Use this data and acquired intuition to prioritize, plan, and scope our product roadmap.
- Work with Marketing to devise new ways to tell great stories throughout the user lifecycle, and across our site, product, help guides and other channels.
- Create new patterns that are intuitive, practical, and convergent. Evolve our design system intentionally as we scale.

Skills You'll Need To Bring



- You have well-rounded skills and experience to run projects independently end to end. 5+ years of working experience.
- You seek to understand the needs of customers then explore and advocate for the strongest user experiences to solve their problems
- You enjoy untangling vague conceptual problems and have a sharp intuition for the most accessible mental models and flows, so users can immediately start gaining value out of the product.
- You create clear, intuitive, and visually appealing human interfaces

title: Product Designer
description:
About Your Role 👀

As the second Product Designer at Pogo, you'll help lead the product design and creative direction for our new consumer insights product, which allows brands/retailers to connect with millions of purchase-verified consumers. This platform will ultimately be used by some of the largest companies in the world.

Specifically, you will:



- Design core product experiences end-to-end, from early exploration through launch and iteration for our up-and-coming B2B platform and consumer app with 3 million users (and growing)
- Craft polished, delightful interfaces that build trust and showcase the power of our data and AI technology
- Sweat the details - layout, typography, spacing, color, motion, interactions
- Help define the product roadmap and lay the foundations for our design language, systems, and culture. 
- Find creative ways to ship high-quality work in a fast-paced, often ambiguous, startup environment
- Be 1 of 2 designers (for now), working cross-functionally with engineering and GTM

💎 We're looking for the best talent out there, so we're offering above-market salaries & equity.

About You 👩‍🚀



- Experience designing software products. 
- Bonus if you’ve done this at a startup, or have designed AI interactions before!
- Bonus if you have experience designing enterprise-grade products. 
- You design quickly and efficiently, using Figma to gain super powers and reach “escape velocity design”. When needed, you make near-term tradeoffs and take shortcuts - even though you have strong design vision and awareness of how to improve the product later. 
- You’re a design nerd at heart. You have a very high bar for design quality and strong opinions about what “great” looks like. You actively seek out the best-designed best products/designers, constantly collecting references from Twitter, Mobbin, and beyond. And you bring that level of rigor and polish into your own work. 
- You actively use LLMs like as ChatGPT or Claude in your design workflow. 
- You’re relentless in pursuing the best solution - willing to explore, iterate, and even scrap a lot of your own work if it means creating a stronger product. 
- You’re a full-stack designer. You've designed experiences from scratch and know how to bring it to life working cross-functionally with product and engineering. 
- You have strong product intuition and have a knack for creating experiences that index on simplicity and clarity. At the same time, you're willing to re-consider your initial intuition as you get more user data. 

Why you might be excited about this opportunity 🙌



- Work on the design for an up-and-coming enterprise product. Our enterprise demand is growing, and we are in the early stages of building a product that will ultimately be used by some of the largest companies in the world. You’ll use qualitative interviews and direct customer feedback to shape product decisions and design solutions tailored to enterprise needs. 
- Design matters a lot to us.

title: UI/UX Designer
description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

Movement changes lives — and for nearly 50 years, Balanced Body has led the world in Pilates equipment and education, pairing mindful movement with world-class engineering. From our solar-powered headquarters in Sacramento, we manufacture premium equipment that helps people feel better and move more freely

We're growing our marketing team and looking for a creative, sharp, strategically-minded UI/UX Product Designer to help shape how people experience Balanced Body online.

A note on the role: this is a design role first and foremost — not software development. You'll own the end-to-end visual and interactive design of our digital products, from user research and wireframing through high-fidelity prototypes. You'll also handle final front-end implementation and visual customization in our CMS platforms (WordPress and Shopify) — but you won't be writing backend code.

You'll report to the Marketing Manager and partner closely with our web development team, serving as the crucial link that turns your designs into flawless, functioning reality.

What You'll Do



- Design Execution — Craft polished, high-fidelity mockups and interactive prototypes in Figma with clean user flows, strong visual hierarchy, and refined aesthetics.
- Ecommerce Experience Design — Design and optimize PDPs, collection pages, navigation, merchandising, and conversion-focused landing pages, meeting WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA accessibility and responsive design standards.
- Analytics & Iteration — Dig into analytics, heatmaps, and session recordings to spot friction points, form hypotheses, and drive iterative UX improvements.
- UX Writing & Microcopy — Own the words that guide the journey: CTAs, error messages, modals, onboarding, and tooltips.
- Design Implementation — Manage the look and feel of our web properties, customizing responsive layouts in WordPress and Shopify to match approved Figma prototypes and design systems.
- Continuous UX Research — Run ongoing user research, usability testing, and heuristic evaluations to keep our platforms grounded in UX best practice.
- Cross-Functional Balancing — Act as creative consultant across marketing, development, and SEO — making agile adjustments without compromising design integrity.
- Visual Asset Creation — Produce polished marketing assets: banners, icons, UI components, and promotional graphics.

Requirements

What You Bring



- Experience: 5+ years in a dedicated UI/UX or Product Design role, comfortable owning timelines and major deliverables independently.
- Education: Bachelor's in a design field (Interaction Design, Visual Communication, Graphic Design, HCI) 
- Portfolio: End-to-end product thinking — UX workflows, interaction design, responsive structures, and refined final execution. A trained eye for type, color, and hierarchy is a must.
- Systems Thinking: Deep understanding of component-based design systems, mobile-first design, and adapting high-fidelity work across breakpoints

title: Product Designer
description:
About Calvis

- Calvis is making the trillion-dollar physical security industry AI-native. Today the industry is outdated, fragmented, and run on pen and paper. With Calvis, Humans + AI work together to secure the world.
- Our marketplace connects businesses with vetted security guards who work every shift using our AI copilot. It briefs them, takes their reports, and helps them do a great job. Meanwhile, every shift generates data that continuously makes our AI better.
- We enhance guards with robots and AI video monitoring, making Calvis the only all-in-one security offering on the market.
- Clients across the country, from critical infrastructure to manufacturing facilities, trust Calvis to help keep them safe.


Why join?

- Very small team, in person, in office. Work directly with the CEO and CTO.
- The business has grown fast over the last year, and our growth rate is only accelerating.
- Complete ownership and autonomy. You own what you work on, end to end, and you decide how to build it. We have plans, but autonomy is the point: it means looking around corners and building for what's coming before it's on our roadmap.
- Your work ships fast and lands in the real world with real guards.
- Everything is still early. You'd be our first designer — what Calvis looks and feels like from here is yours to define.


The role

- Design how AI shows up in the physical world: the copilot a guard talks to all night, the alerts a business acts on, and guards, robots, and sensors working together on a live site.
- Own products end-to-end. You get to understand the guards and customers who use what you build, figure out what they need, and ship.
- Work across every surface we have: web dashboard, native iOS and Android apps, and internal ops tools.
- Build the design system, the brand, and the quality bar — the foundation everyone hired after you builds on.
- Take what's working and raise it. Our products have real usage and real revenue but have never had a designer. You'll iterate against live usage and turn working v1s into experiences people love.


Who you are

- Worked at a high-growth startup before. You thrive in chaos, change, and uncertainty.
- You work hard, and you're wired in. The business, the problems, and the thing you're building stay on your mind because you actually care.
- You design with AI every day and treat staying at the frontier as part of the job. You're constantly learning from new models, tactics, and workflows, and folding them into how you work.
- Product mindset paired with craft. You dig into what users are actually struggling with, structure complex operational products, and make them beautiful.
- You prototype in code, or want to. We move too fast for static mocks alone.

title: Product Designer
description:
About The Role

Hinge Health is a company that recognizes the value of design – as a Product Designer, you’ll join a tight-knit, collaborative team of designers who care deeply about creating cohesive and intuitive product experiences. Our team is at the center of solving impactful problems for millions of members who are managing their joint and muscle health, and making a meaningful difference in their lives.

In this role, you’ll lead the design of our member communication ecosystem, ensuring members are informed and supported throughout their care journey. You’ll own the end-to-end design for proactive outreach, including notification surfaces, preference management, and the Connect tab which helps connect members with their care team anywhere and anytime through visit scheduling and messaging. About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work



- We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
- Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
- We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
- Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.
- We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways we’ve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About The Role:

We're looking for a Product Designer to help shape the experience for the developers and teams who build on LangChain. You'll work across our core product surfaces, and depending on where the need is greatest, that could include how developers get from first signup to real production usage, as well as deeper platform workflows like debugging, evaluation, and observability.

The common thread is developers doing technical, often high-stakes work, and needing an interface that gets out of their way. You'll partner with engineering, product, and other designers to figure out where the friction is and design your way out of it.

What you'll do:



- Build a deep understanding of how developers actually use LangChain's products through interviews and feedback sessions so your design decisions are grounded in real behavior and address user needs
- Own the full design arc on your features — from early concepts to polished, shipped work
- Work across a range of product areas and design initiatives as priorities shift
- Collaborate closely with product, engineering and other key stakeholders to ship new features quickly

What you'll bring:



- 3+ years of fullstack product design experience ideally working on developer tools, AI, or complex SaaS products
- Sharp eye for detail, with a strong foundation across user-centered design, interaction design, and visual craft
- A track record of solving hard interaction design problems, particularly around dense technical data
- Data-driven decision making - you are comfortable driving user research, both with internal stakeholders and external customers, and using what you learn to inform your designs

Cricut® makes smart cutting machines that work with an easy-to-use app, an ever-growing collection of materials, and crafting essentials to help you design and personalize almost anything — custom cards, unique apparel, everyday items, and so much more.


We believe everyone is born creative. We’re a diverse tapestry of thinkers, dreamers, givers, DIYers, handi-workers, artisans, and forever and always architects of things.


At Cricut, we place the power of handmade into the hands of all. We give you beautiful, easy-to-master tools so you can make something unique, remarkable, perfect. We surround you with ideas, community, inspiration, and encouragement to take your creativity further than you ever imagined. And as a community, we celebrate the exhilarating act of making every single day. 


So, make that handcrafted card that feels like a hug. Design a shirt for fun, for family, or for a full-blown business. Craft with a passion or for a purpose. Make something big and bold, itsy-bitsy, amazingly ambitious, or just plain silly. Whatever you make, just make your heart out. Because here’s the remarkable truth: When we all make together, we make all things possible.



Let’s make.

The UX team at Cricut is responsible for user research, interaction design and visual design of software applications across desktop and mobile platforms. We design intuitive, easy-to-use software that inspires our customers, and helps them design and make unique, personalized projects. 


The team is uniquely positioned – with direct connections to the executive team and CEO - and we collaborate across the organization to ensure hardware, content, materials, and software all work together to deliver awesome experiences. Our UX team members come from varied backgrounds and experience; all of us were drawn to the mission of empowering every person to be creative. 


As a Lead UX Designer within the UX team at Cricut, you’ll lead the creation of thoughtful and compelling user experiences to elevate the brand and introduce Cricut to a wider audience. You’ll provide design thought leadership and work on complex and interesting UX projects spanning multiple platforms including mobile and desktop software. You’ll be a hands-on contributor committed to creating industry-leading experiences for some of the most engaged user groups you’ll ever encounter. Put aside your assumptions and drop us a line…this opportunity is not to be missed. ­ 


Responsibilities 



- Lead the design work for software applications for both desktop and mobile devices across a range of operating systems. 
- Reinforce a learning mindset: Participate in user research and A/B testing, advocate for our users at every step of the way, and leverage findings artfully to continuously improve designs. 
- Bring a keen understanding of our users’ motivations, goals and needs to help define new features, functions and products. 
- Extend and evolve our UX design language to craft elegant and

title: Founding Product Designer
description:
About The Role

This is a first-ever design hire at a seed-stage neurotechnology startup building a cognitive fitness tracker — think of it as Strava for the brain. The product surfaces trends and insights on mental clarity, cognitive load, stress, and more, with a mission to make brain health accessible, measurable, and actionable.

There is no design system to inherit, no style guide to reference, and no established design language for this ambient product category — because nothing quite like it exists yet. You'll build everything from the ground up, working directly with the Founder to own the full design surface from early concept through shipped product.

We're looking for a bit of a mad artist: someone who takes risks, challenges conventions, brings a multidisciplinary perspective, stays deeply curious, and pushes back when something feels wrong.

What You'll Do



- Rapidly generate and iterate on design directions, testing ideas with early users to drive engagement
- Build and maintain the company's design system entirely from scratch
- Lead user research to surface unmet needs and validate product hypotheses
- Collaborate closely with engineers to ship implementable, high-quality interfaces
- Define the visual and interaction language for a voice-first, ambient product category
- Partner with the Founder on product strategy — shaping what gets built, not just how it looks

What We're Looking For

Requirements (dealbreakers):



- 2+ years of design experience at an early-stage consumer startup
- Proven track record shipping full-scale consumer apps end-to-end — from concept to production, not just components or marketing sites
- Experience building and maintaining a design system (not just handing off Figma files)
- Authorized to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Required skills & mindset:



- Proficiency with Figma and strong design systems tooling
- Hands-on experience with user research and rapid prototyping to validate hypotheses
- Product thinker first — you shape what gets built, not just how it looks
- Comfortable working directly with a founder and influencing product direction
- Core contributor to a team that built something people genuinely love from the ground up

Nice to haves:



- Experience with voice-first, ambient, or AI-assisted product design
- Background in consumer health, fitness, wearables, or related domains

Compensation & Benefits



- Salary: $150,000 – $200,000 USD annually
- Meaningful equity package
- Health benefits
- Flexible PTO

Location

This role is on-site in San Francisco, CA. Visa sponsorship is not available — candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.

You'll join a small, talented product team designing consumer-facing experiences built around gaming culture and creator-driven communities. Designing across both desktop and mobile, you'll shape polished, accessible experiences seen by millions of gamers.

What Lumion does
Lumion is the all-in-one operating system for trade and technical schools. We power the entire institution: AI-driven lead generation and conversion, enrollment, financial aid, student lifecycle management, and tuition payments. Most schools are still stitching together five or six disconnected tools to do what our platform handles.


America has a massive skilled trades shortage and the schools that train electricians, welders, and nurses are the bottleneck. We're backed by TTV Capital and Tusk Venture Partners.
Why this role matters


You would be Lumion's first dedicated product designer. Until now, design has been done by the founders, product managers, and engineers. That carried us a long way, and it is no longer enough.


Our engineers build with AI-native workflows, so the constraint on the product is no longer how fast we can write code. It is how fast we can figure out exactly what to build and make it excellent. That is design work, and right now it is our bottleneck.


The people who use our platform are admissions directors, school owners, and finance staff who live in it all day, and students making one of the bigger financial decisions of their lives. Most software in this industry was built a decade ago and looks like it. You get to set the bar for what great looks like in this market.


The work
You will own design across the entire platform.


Product design end to end. You take features from PRD to shipped: user flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and specs engineers can build from without guessing. You will work directly with the CEO and CTO in design sessions and own the outcome.


Prototypes. Before engineering commits to a build, we want a working prototype in front of real schools. You will produce clickable, testable prototypes fast and use what you learn to sharpen the spec before a line of production code gets written.


The design system. The platform spans lead management, enrollment, messaging, scheduling, payments, and reporting, and it grew fast. You will build the component library and interaction patterns that make it feel like one product, and that let engineers ship good UI without a designer in the room.


AI interfaces. Schools use Lumion to configure and supervise AI agents that text, email, and call prospective students. Designing how a non-technical admissions director sets up an agent, reviews its conversations, and learns to trust it is new territory with little prior art. You will define those patterns.


Student surfaces. Enrollment applications, document signing, and tuition payments, mostly on a phone. These flows handle real money and real decisions, and they have to be effortless.

The Forbes brand reaches more than 140 million people monthly worldwide through its trusted journalism, signature ForbesLive events and 49 licensed local editions in 81 countries. 
The Forbes Editorial Art Team sits at the intersection of journalism and digital innovation, shaping the visual identity of success and influence that define the cultural conversation. From the split-second hook of a short-form social story to the prestige of our global franchises like 30 Under 30 and the Billionaires List, we turn data and reporting into compelling digital narratives. Our designers collaborate across the newsroom, product, and live event teams to tell holistic, platform-first stories that meet our audience exactly where they are. We are looking for a Social Designer with a visual journalism mindset, someone who can distill complex power dynamics and business trends into high-impact digital content. Reporting to the Design Director and embedded daily with the Social Strategy team, you will translate Forbes’ deep-dive reporting into thumb-stopping visual narratives. The ideal candidate is a conceptual thinker who doesn't just follow trends but anticipates them, leveraging emerging AI tools and design best practices to keep the Forbes brand at the forefront of the feed.
Note: An online portfolio demonstrating a proven success in social-first storytelling is required for consideration.
Responsibilities:

- Shortform Visual Content Creation: Design narrative-driven graphics, data visualizations and photo-centric stories for social-first features and Forbes major franchises (e.g., 30 Under 30).
- Animation and Motion Design: Transform static editorial assets into high-impact animations for social feeds, ranging from data visualizations and kinetic typography to list reveals and video covers.
- Platform Optimization: Translate long-form web content into platform-specific formats (Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, etc.), ensuring all assets meet technical specs, safe zones, and aspect ratio requirements.
- Iterative Design: Use social performance metrics and engagement data to refine visual formats and experiment with new storytelling techniques.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with design, photo, video, editorial and social strategy teams to ensure a "social-first" approach to editorial packages.
- AI & Tool Integration: Drive production efficiencies by integrating AI and specialized Figma plugins into your daily workflow to accelerate visual ideation and output.
- Brand Quality Control: Maintain rigorous alignment with Forbes’ visual id

title: Model Designer
description:
About The Team

The Core Models team shapes how our models interact with people. We view the model as the product itself, aiming for intuitive experiences that exceed user expectations and feel like magic.

About The Role

As a Model Designer, you’ll have an outsized impact on how our models interact and resonate with users.

You’ll strike a delicate balance between maximizing the model’s capabilities, reading in between the lines in user queries to understand how best to help, and upholding user trust.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about the intersection of design, technology, and user experience — and are up for the challenge of defining new human-AI interaction paradigms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you’ll join a small team in evolving and expanding the model design function. You will:



- Collaborate closely with researchers to understand, predict, and design model behavior.
- Partner with product managers and designers across the company to ensure a cohesive voice and approach.
- Proactively identify ways to improve our models based on product sense, user feedback, quantitative insights, and the research roadmap.
- Come up with creative strategies for collecting high-quality data.
- Do whatever needs to be done to make our models better.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You



- Possess exceptional taste, creativity, and writing skills, allowing you to craft responses that delight users.
- Don’t mind ambiguity — you’re happy to throw yourself into a new, unfamiliar environment, build relationships, define a problem, and make progress.
- Love experimentation, and are willing to test and reject new ideas when the results don’t pan out.
- Exhibit high levels of empathy and self-awareness required to serve everyone in the world.
- Enjoy tackling profound and often philosophical questions while always driving towards clarity.
- Demonstrate technical intuition to learn how changes in data can affect overall model behavior.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Poli

title: Product Designer II - Uber Eats, Offers Consumer Experiences
description:
About The Role

Uber Eats makes it easy to get the food you love delivered. You will create delightful consumer experiences that redefine how millions discover value. By building industry-leading discovery and optimizing affordability, you will craft innovative solutions that serve an incredibly diverse global community.

As a Product Designer II on the Offers team within the Ads & Offers org, you will play a central role in reimagining what an offer can be. You will flex your skills across project vision and strategy to deliver immediate impact, shaping a global platform where inspired design and smart monetization empower merchants and delight users everywhere.

What You Will Do



-  Own design problems from beginning to end, from the initial concept through to shipping and beyond 
-  Create wireframes, visual designs, and prototypes to address complex UX problems 
-  Design systems to create simple, elegant experiences 
-  Collaborate with product to define requirements, not just translate them into design 
-  Identify future opportunities and work as a key thought partner with your counterparts in product, engineering, and operations 
-  Partner with our UX research team to better understand our customers' needs 

 Basic Qualifications 



-  3+ years of Product Design experience 
-  A portfolio showcasing high-quality designs and problem-solving ability 

 Preferred Qualifications 



-  Consumer mobile design experience is a plus 
-  Strong written and verbal communication skills 
-  Excellent presentation and storytelling skills 
-  Ability to manage stakeholders, requirements, and deliverables independently 
-  Experience working on consumer facing marketplaces or commerce 
-  Experience working on a global product 
-  Experience creating highly accessible products 
-  Ability to create high-fidelity prototypes 

~~ ~~

For New York City, NY-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $153,000 per year - USD $170,000 per year.

For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $153,000 per year - USD $170,000 per year.

For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

Ready to Ride?

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook - it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves - we'd love to hear from you.

You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this rol

description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About The Role

We’re hiring a Product Designer for our Benefits team to design and launch a new product offering at Gusto. Our focus in Benefits is simple: help small businesses and their employees get access to better quality care at more affordable rates—in other words, we make benefits work harder for small businesses.

Benefits is a notoriously complex space, full of confusing choices, high stakes, and fragmented experiences across employers, employees, carriers, and brokers. In this role, you’ll partner closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Data Science, CX, Operations, and Sales to turn that complexity into experiences that feel clear, human, and trustworthy—from end-to-end journeys to the underlying systems that power them.

This is an opportunity to shape a new part of Gusto’s Benefits offering and deliver meaningful, tangible impact for small businesses and the people who rely on them.

About The Team

Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We're a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don't care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference. We believe great design can make hard things possible, even delightful.

We are building an AI-native design organization — and we mean that seriously. We're looking for designers who are already working this way: using AI to prototype ideas quickly, shorten customer feedback loops, and ship quality UX directly to customers. This isn't a future aspiration — it's how we work now, and it's changing what the design role looks like at Gusto and across the industry.

Here’s What You’ll Do Day-to-day

description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

You’ll partner closely with cross-functional teams to design intuitive, high-impact solutions that balance user needs with business goals, and help customers expand their use of the Figma ecosystem.

This role calls for a systems thinker and skilled visual designer who can move fluidly between strategy, storytelling, and execution. You’ll simplify complex workflows, contribute to product strategy, and design scalable systems that strengthen the relationship between users and Figma—always with a strong sense of craft and user advocacy.

This opportunity applies to openings of varying seniority levels across our Monetization and Growth teams. We’ll discuss more specifics about open roles during the interview process.

- Help deliver and refine clear storytelling around product needs and opportunities

- Contribute to our design org’s culture by participating in design critiques, mentoring peers, and sharing best practices across teams

We're looking for a Creative Lead to bring rabbit's visual identity to life through thoughtful design, compelling campaign creative, and exceptional execution. description:
You will spend your time combining great design with incredible technology. As a user interface designer at SARJ you will be responsible for taking the amazing products our engineers create and building them into something that is beautiful and user friendly. You'll be developing your ideas into mockups, wireframes, and front-end code.

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
- 4 years of interaction design experience in product design or UX design.
- Include a portfolio, website, or any other relevant link to your work in your resume (providing a viewable link or access instructions).

Preferred qualifications:



- Experience utilizing AI tools, including prototyping and building with AI, to ship fully realized, highly-polished features and explore the future of conversational or automated payments.
- Experience working with Google Ads or equivalent platforms.
- Experience working closely with Security and Privacy, Safety, and Legal teams.

About The Job

At Google, we "Focus on the user and all else will follow." Our Interaction Designers transform complex tasks into intuitive, easy-to-use experiences for billions of people. From creating user flows and wireframes to building mockups and prototypes, you will envision and bring product experiences to life with an inspired, refined, and magical feel. You will join our multi-disciplinary UX team, collaborating with Engineering and Product Management, leveraging user insights to create industry-leading products.

As an Interaction Designer, you'll apply user-centered design methods to craft industry-leading user experiences from concept to execution, working with design partners to evolve the Google design language to build beautiful, innovative products.

At the same time, we ensure that advertisers are able to navigate complex policies without major interruption to their work and correct mistakes when they occur.

From crafting intricate information graphics that demystify complex machine learning concepts, to producing high-quality videos and graphic design assets, you will shape how both users and internal stakeholders understand our products. To achieve this, you will actively integrate AI tools and prompt engineering into the day-to-day workflow, using technology to amplify creative process, accelerate prototyping, and discover new ways of working.

title: Product Designer
description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

Imagine yourself in the 1970s or 80s thinking through how computing should look and feel for people who had never seen one before. That's what we're trying to do at Notion — make software that feels timeless, with the craftsmanship of German cameras, playfulness of Japanese toys, and mass appeal of Coca-Cola. We have no end of fascinating challenges that can only be solved by someone with innate product & UX sense, technical aptitude, great taste, and impeccable craft.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve



- Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential.
- Craft every detail of new product features, from idea to UX to pixel-perfect execution.
- Run projects end to end with engineers to drive your vision to the ship line.
- Partner closely with our Customer Experience, Sales, and Customer Success teams to understand what each of our diverse user segments need, want, and love about Notion. Use this data and acquired intuition to prioritize, plan, and scope our product roadmap.
- Work with Marketing to devise new ways to tell great stories throughout the user lifecycle, and across our site, product, help guides and other channels.
- Create new patterns that are intuitive, practical, and convergent. Evolve our design system intentionally as we scale.

Skills You'll Need To Bring



- You have well-rounded skills and experience to run projects independently end to end. 5+ years of working experience.
- You seek to understand the needs of customers then explore and advocate for the strongest user experiences to solve their problems
- You enjoy untangling vague conceptual problems and have a sharp intuition for the most accessible mental models and flows, so users can immediately start gaining value out of the product.
- You create clear, intuitive, and visually appealing human interfaces

title: Designer
description:
Amca is building America’s new industrial base. Since the 1990s, our ability to build new aviation and military systems and maintain the ones we already have has eroded. Today, the gap between what the nation needs to produce and what it is capable of producing is the largest it has been in generations.

To help close that gap, Amca rapidly develops and manufactures new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. Today, we operate seven factories nationwide, including our advanced prototyping and testing headquarters in El Segundo, and deliver avionics, hydraulic, and electrical components for platforms such as the F-35, F-16, F/A-18, 737MAX, 787, A320neo, A321, Mk-48, and M1 Abrams.

Amca’s Designer will be responsible for continually bringing our aesthetic vision to life across every imaginable medium, using and building on a new brand system developed with our friends at Day Job. You will work closely with our Senior Designer and VP of Strategy and Business to

- Conceptualizing and designing maximalist posters that capture the Amca ethos for display in our multiple offices and factories
- Designing poster-like slide decks for customers with a degree of personalization that almost feels unbelievable
- Creating merch for our brands that captures the essence of their respective cultures, which have been built over many decades
- Creating custom marketing collateral for each of our flagship brands: physical brochures, physical objects, packing materials

- You are an excellent graphic designer (as a baseline)

- You feel like more designers need to play with the medium in which they express their ideas, rather than constraining themselves to just one

- You’re comfortable with campaign conceptualization, not just design itself
- You’re comfortable operationalizing your ideas (sourcing suppliers, external partners) when they require additional help
- You can work with time pressure across multiple projects, and make thoughtful trade-offs to meet external deadlines

You Get Bonus Points If



- You can spin up webpages yourself without the help of a web developer, whether because you can code yourself or because you’re good at using AI tools
- You know your way around Blender, Cinema4D or Maya
- You have illustration chops

This role is in-person in our new, Charlap Hyman & Herrero designed office and factory in El Segundo, in the heart of Southern California’s aviation industry.

title: Product Designer
description:
Wevise is on a mission to level the playing field in tech. Through direct programming and partnerships with nonprofits supporting underserved and disadvantaged people to enter and advance in the technology industry, we provide access to mentors, training and educational opportunities, and careers.

Our goals



- Support underserved and disadvantaged people to enter and thrive in the technology industry
- Partner with organizations who need mentorship and career placement programs to complement their main programming, helping them to better serve their beneficiaries
- Support companies in finding the right, often diverse, candidates

We have two programs a free, on-demand mentorship platform that allows people to request mentorship based on specific needs, interests, background, and experience. Mentors and mentees can specify their interest in short, medium, and long-term mentorship. Mentors choose one or more mentees that resonate with them from a curated list of five mentorship requests. Although the platform is open and free to all, we are focused on supporting underserved and disadvantaged people. Mentors and mentees are matched with people who have overcome similar barriers.

Our second program is called the TechPath Alliance, which is a city-focused program currently being piloted in Chicago, IL. The initiative brings together nonprofits and for-profits to collaboratively run a 6 month mentoring and career development program for underserved emerging tech professionals.

,

Volunteer Product Designer (Remote)

Help design technology that expands access to mentorship and career opportunities. We're looking for a product designer passionate about social impact to own UX and UI for our mentorship platform — from user flows and wireframes to polished, accessible interfaces in Figma. You'll work directly with our Lead Product Designer and technology and marketing teams to shape what we build. 5–10 hours/week, fully remote, flexible schedule.

description:
🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!

Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.

As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. description:
Junior Visual Designer — Print & Digital
Hybrid | Western Suburbs of Chicago
Full-time | 3 days per week in office
Salary: based on experience and portfolio


About Jak Creative Design
Jak Creative Design is a woman-owned, independent creative agency based in the western suburbs of Chicago.
For nearly three decades, we’ve partnered with startups, nonprofits, and Fortune 100 brands to create thoughtful, design-driven work across print, digital, branding, and campaign systems.
We’re a small, experienced team that values strong relationships, smart thinking, collaboration, and creative that performs in the real world.
Our work often moves quickly and includes a high volume of detailed deliverables, so accuracy, organization, and follow-through matter just as much as creative thinking.


The Role
We’re looking for a motivated, detail-oriented Junior Visual Designer who is early in their career and ready to grow through hands-on agency experience.
This role is designed for a recent graduate or designer with up to two years of professional experience. We will also consider candidates with less than one year of experience who demonstrate strong design fundamentals, a thoughtful portfolio, and a willingness to learn.
You’ll work closely with senior creative leadership and the broader team to develop and execute marketing materials across print and digital, with a strong emphasis on direct mail, campaign creative, presentations, email, and production-ready design.
You do not need to know everything on day one. You should, however, have strong fundamentals, good judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to take feedback and apply it thoughtfully.


This role includes working within:

- Established brand guidelines
- Campaign and layout systems
- Direct mail and print production requirements

- Multiple timelines and changing priorities


What You’ll Do

- Design and update materials across print and digital, including direct mail, email, web, presentations, social media, and display advertising
- Translate creative direction into clear, polished, on-brand work
- Develop concepts and layouts with guidance from senior team members
- Adapt existing campaign systems across formats, audiences, offers, and versions
- Prepare accurate, production-ready files for print and digital use
- Build and revise direct mail pieces, including envelopes, letters, inserts, and supporting campaign materials
- Make revisions based on internal and client feedback
- Collaborate with designers, project managers, account teams, copywriters, and production partners
- Manage multiple assignments while staying organized and meeting deadlines
- Participate in brainstorms, creative reviews, and internal presentations
- Ask thoughtful questions, communicate clearly, and take ownership of assigned work
What You Bring

- Zero to two years of professional design experience, including internships, freelance work, or relevant in-house or agency experie

title: Studio Designer
description:
Studio Designer
You’re the person who makes sure beautiful ideas leave the building flawlessly.
You love the details, file names, specs, color profiles, bleeds, versions, all of it. When something goes to a media partner or print vendor, you want it buttoned-up, on spec, and on time.
At Zimmerman Agency, we’re looking for a Studio Designer with strong technical and production design skills to be a key part of our creative process.
What you’ll do

- Prepare and finalize production-ready files for print, OOH, digital, and social
- Handle pre-press tasks: setting up bleeds, crops, color profiles, imposition needs, and printer requirements
- Version, resize, and adapt existing designs across multiple formats and specs
- Ensure all deliverables meet technical requirements for print shops, media partners, and digital platforms
- Maintain organized file structures, naming conventions, and version control
- Collaborate closely with the design and creative teams to ensure work is accurate, consistent, and on-brand
- Perform quality control checks on files before they go out the door
- Problem-solve with vendors and internal teams when specs change or issues arise
What you bring

- Proven technical design / production design experience (agency or in-house studio experience a plus)
- Strong abilities in Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat for pre-press checks)
- Solid understanding of:
- Pre-press and print production (CMYK vs RGB, resolution, bleeds, safety, etc.)
- Digital file prep for web and social (sizes, formats, compression, platform specs)
- Detail-obsessed and highly organized, you take pride in clean files and tight workflows
- Comfortable working with templates, guidelines, and brand systems
- Accountable and reliable, deadlines matter and you don’t let things slip
- Strong communicator who can work with designers, project managers, and vendors to get files right
- Positive, collaborative attitude
Why you’ll love working here

- You’ll be central to getting the work out into the world, your fingerprints will be on everything
- A tight, collaborative creative team that values the studio role (we know nothing ships without you)
- A fun, travel-focused agency environment with varied clients and formats
- On-site in Tallahassee, FL, working shoulder-to-shoulder with designers and creatives
- A stable role with room to grow your skills in both print and digital production

We want students who are motivated, creative, and strategic – natural leaders seeking to drive results in a team-based environment.

- Combination of classroom sessions and on-the-job training 
- Relationship with a mentor to guide learning in the new role 
- Interactive presentations from a variety of senior leaders in the company 
- An open and inclusive learning environment with fellow associates

Designers focus on every aspect of product development, from fabric and trim selection to editing how the garment fits on live models.

- Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA

- Detail-oriented with excellent time management and organizational skills   
- Career-driven, strong work ethic and high-performance standards   
- Strong communication and presentation skills   
- A collaborative approach to working with cross-functional partners to achieve the vision of the brand  
- A strong desire for adventure & curiosity   
- Ability to adapt and work in a fast-paced, structured environment  
- Desire to learn & hunger for more!

Our mission is to help organizations turn any growth idea into reality.

- Our community includes 11,000+ customers, 150+ integration partners, 125+ agencies, 50+ Clay clubs, and 30k members on Slack.

- All employees can work for free with world-class coaches who specialize in creativity, management, and more.
- Our operating principles — including negative maintenance and non-attached action — guide our work. Read more about them here.
- Read about us in the NYT, Forbes, First Round Review, and more.

Hear from our employees directly on our Glassdoor page!

Product Design @ Clay

Clay is at an inflection point — $100M+ ARR, Series C, and a rapidly expanding customer base. We're building a dedicated growth pod to systematically accelerate acquisition, activation, and retention. You'll be the design lead for that pod, helping us turn growth hypotheses into experiments, and experiments into durable product experiences.

As a senior–staff growth designer, you'll operate in two modes: embedded partner within the growth pod, and trusted consultant to other teams who need to run their own growth experiments. You'll create quick wins through experimentation while simultaneously building the systems and patterns that make future experimentation faster, more consistent, and less dependent on bespoke design.

Questions We're Asking & Exploring



- How do we quickly gather quantitative data and qualitative signal to identify our biggest growth levers — and use those insights to decide how to act on them?
- How can growth experiments ship quickly without creating long-term design debt or inconsistent surfaces?
- How do we design growth surfaces (onboarding flows, carousels, empty states, upgrade prompts) as modular, configurable components — so running a new variant means changing content or parameters, not rebuilding from scratch?
- How do we know when a growth solution has proven itself enough to become a shared pattern? What does it take for something to graduate from a one-off experiment into the design system?

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. description:
About Us

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.

About The Design Team

We’re a small, high-craft team of six working at the intersection of research, invention, and product thinking. We build consumer and B2B experiences used by millions across 150+ markets — and a lot of the work is genuinely novel: inventing how someone talks to an AI tutor, what feedback feels like when you’re learning out loud, and how progress should be measured and celebrated.

We stay close to learners through prototyping, interviews, betas, and experiments. We take craft seriously, iterate fast, and value a high-trust critique-and-build culture. We have something to prove — and design awards to win.

Role & responsibilities

Speak’s enterprise product is still early, but the problem is big: companies need to know whether their teams are actually building language proficiency, where learners are getting stuck, and what interventions will help. You’ll help define the tools they use to launch programs, understand progress, spot risks, and prove that language learning is working.



- Shape the strategy and design of our company-facing product — the admin, reporting, and account experiences the L&D managers who buy Speak rely on to launch, run, and prove their programs

- Set the design foundation for a surface that's still early — closer to 0-to-1 than operating a mature product
- Quickly set up prototypes in AI tools or code to communicate concepts, build alignment, and pressure-test real experiences
- Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, GTM, and Customer Success — translating what customers need to buy, launch, renew, and expand into product experiences that actually work
- Feel comfortable and creative in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment
